realm-fort-s1#0.notes: Realm castle: fat cream keep with a big blue cone and two blue-coned towers at the back centre, packed half-timbered red-roofed houses, thick crenellated front wall with a twin-towered gatehouse centred over the entry cell; dense, tall, cute; reads on light and dark at 1:1

restless-fort-s1#0.notes: Restless churchyard: tall crooked slate cathedral with violet roofs and a bell tower, crooked manor, bone-white domed mausoleum, crypts, tombstones, iron gate between lantern pillars centred; spooky-cute, no gore; narrower (about 150 px) but tall

horde-fort-s1#0.notes: Warlord's Hold: tall riveted tin boss hall under a hazard-yellow roof, wooden lookout tower, yellow-roofed tin shacks, spotted hide tent, scrap heaps, a thick stake wall with a horned ox skull gate centred; chunky and dense

horde-camp-a#0.notes: Horde warcamp: big spotted hide boss tent at the back centre, yellow-roofed tin shacks and scrap heaps packed round it, a crooked stake fence with the horned ox skull gate centred; same palette as the Hold but clearly the lighter stage (no tin hall, no tower)

lost-world-fort-a#0.notes: Lost World town: huge thatched longhouse at the back centre, plump spotted-hide huts, red-painted bone totem, drying racks, basalt stones, a log fence and a giant dinosaur-skull gate centred over the entry cell; the cutest of the set

restless-camp-a#0.notes: near duplicate of restless-fort-s1 (same cathedral, mausoleum and gate): the style image copied the layout, so the camp stage would not read as smaller

realm-camp-a#0.notes: reads as a second castle: the round keep with a big blue cone copied from the fort, so the camp and fort stages are hard to tell apart

realm-camp-b#0.notes: Realm village: white half-timbered chapel with a blue roof and steeple at the back centre, chunky red-roofed cottages packed round it, well, haystacks, a low plank fence with a small blue-roofed gate centred; clearly the village stage beside the castle

restless-camp-b#0.notes: Restless graveyard: huddle of crooked violet-roofed houses round a little slate chapel with a bell gable, crypts, tombstones, a bare dead tree, iron railings with lantern posts and a small gate centred; no cathedral or mausoleum, so it reads as the camp stage
